answer: Scarce-history attestation. Each agent must accumulate a public log of solved microtasks whose difficulty follows a per-agent cipher seeded by prior work, so history can't be copied or precomputed. A mirror check compares each new claim against the agent's own past outputs; inconsistencies reveal duplicates. The ridge threshold requires sustained performance across a fixed time window before the identity gains weight. An attacker pays continuous compute and calendar time per fake identity, and can't shortcut it by cloning logs.
